lessons: RESOLVED [CARRY]: the scribe_v1 question was never a 'should we switch'. ElevenLabs REMOVED scribe_v1 on 2026-07-09, so captions-only.sh, the skill's headline cheap path, had been unable to transcribe anything for about seven weeks. Upstream helpers/transcribe.py still hardcodes scribe_v1, so this skill must OVERRIDE upstream here rather than defer to it. Lesson: a CARRY phrased as a preference can be hiding a hard breakage; re-derive the question, do not just re-answer it.

RESOLVED [CARRY]: install-hebrew-fonts.sh Debian path. fonts.google.com/download?family=X returns HTTP 200 with 193KB of HTML, so curl -f succeeded, unzip failed, the failure was swallowed by a WARN, and the script printed 'Done.' having installed nothing. Now fetches google/fonts raw TTFs with a magic-byte guard.

RESOLVED [CARRY]: macos-ffmpeg-setup 'option C' and the stale domain-checklist pointers (Step 7 -> Step 9, the nonexistent canonical-BiDi escape hatch, the inert 'on every minor version bump' re-check trigger, now pinned to a HEAD SHA since upstream has no versions at all).

RESOLVED [CARRY]: the per-example dollar totals. Scribe v2 is $0.22/hr, not $0.40, and the ~40% cut was June 2026, not March. Starter is $6, not $5. The $1-3 captions-only band still holds because Claude tokens dominate.

The worst defect this cycle was in code whose prose was entirely correct. burn-hebrew-captions.sh rewrites PlayResY 288 to the real frame height, which silently changes the UNIT MarginV and FontSize are expressed in. A fixed MARGINV=80 therefore meant 31.25% of height in upstream's coordinate space and 4.2% in the rewritten one. Measured on a 1080x1920 render: caption baseline 89px from the bottom, 4.6% of height, buried inside the TikTok UI band that upstream's MarginV=90 exists to clear, while the domain-checklist claimed we RAISED the margin above upstream. Whenever a script rewrites a coordinate system, every constant expressed in it becomes a bug.

Second code-only defect: the python-bidi pre-shape called get_display(line) with no base_dir, so paragraph direction was inferred from the first strong character and any caption starting with a Latin token rendered in reversed word order. Measured: get_display('React הוא מעולה') puts React leftmost; base_dir='R' puts it rightmost. In Israeli tech video that line shape is common, and the script's own self-check example is pure Hebrew, so the failure was invisible to its own verification.

Fixing the geometry BROKE the verification, and only the Expert caught it. The verify-frame crop was a fixed 200px strip 20px above the bottom edge. Once the margin became 31.25%, the captions sat ~600px up and every verification frame on portrait video was empty background, while the script still printed 'MANDATORY VISUAL CHECK'. Lesson: when you move what a check looks at, re-run the check and assert it still sees something. The crop is now derived from MARGINV and FONTSIZE.

Also traced the same unit bug to Outline, Spacing and MarginL/R, which had been left fixed: a 4px outline against a 120px font is a third of upstream's relative stroke (Outline=2 against FontSize=18). All now scale.

The portrait branch first keyed on BASE_H > BASE_W, which gave a 4:5 Instagram feed post a 31% bottom margin it has no UI rail to clear. Now tests for an aspect at least as tall as 9:16. Verified: 1920x1080, 1080x1350 and 1080x1080 all keep the previously shipping ratios, so the landscape lecture case is byte-for-byte unchanged.

The magic-byte guard I first wrote was itself inert: grep BRE/ERE does not expand \xNN, so '^\x00\x01\x00\x00' never matches a real TTF and everything fell through to file(1), which slim images do not ship. Now uses od. Verified both ways: a real TTF reads 00010000 and is accepted, the Google Fonts HTML shell reads 3c21646f and is rejected.

burn-hebrew-captions.sh used to rewrite the SRT passed to --srt in place, so the documented one-line invocation silently overwrote video-use's own master.srt, a paid non-recreatable Scribe artifact. It now sanitizes into a working copy.

Tested and recorded a negative result: FFmpeg documents subtitles shaping=complex as 'required for correct rendering of complex scripts such as Arabic, Hebrew', which makes it look like the supported alternative to the pre-shape. It is not. On a HarfBuzz-enabled ffmpeg 9.0.1, shaping=auto and shaping=complex produced byte-identical frames and an un-pre-shaped Hebrew line still rendered in source byte order. Shaping is glyph substitution, not reordering. Do not re-open this.

CARRY (Expert MAJOR): the main Scribe call posts the whole MP4 (-F file=@VIDEO) while the gap-recovery path correctly extracts audio first. A 3-hour 1080p lecture, the flagship use case, is multiple GB over one multipart POST, after the user has already confirmed billing. Extract to m4a once and reuse for both passes. Needs a live API key to test.

CARRY (Expert MAJOR): nikud. get_display reorders code points, so Hebrew combining marks can detach from their base letter. The skill asserts Scribe rarely emits nikud, yet its own ALWAYS-FILLER lexicon ships nikud forms. Strip combining marks in Step 0 or normalize NFC.

CARRY (Expert MAJOR): Mode B has three different price floors across the skill ($25-60 in the table, $10-300 in the Step 0 consent disclaimer, $5-12 in the Hebrew cost table). The disclaimer is a consent statement and must not contradict the rate table.

The SCRIPT is ground truth and it DOES the pre-shape (its header explains libass doesn't reorder even with libfribidi linked).
